answer: Neighborhood Cutoff. Agents record every counterparty, making a public graph. An identity is admitted only if its edges funnel through at least three sparse, weakly linked clusters—like willow branches fanning from distinct stems. New nodes grafted onto one cluster alone stay quarantined until independent paths open. Forging that topology costs an attacker three separate address populations plus ongoing link maintenance, a crystal structure that is cheap to claim but expensive to keep uncracked. Honest agents dock in the harbor for free.
